Key asks from our side: 1) how revenue split and commission waterfall will be documented in the Marketplace contract, 2) what evidence (purchase records, entitlement manifests) Microsoft will require for downstream invoicing/reconciliation, and 3) standard runbook for activating entitlements and routing invoices.

I attached the initial SOW and a short summary of our internal billing cadence. We also have a shortlist of compliance questions from legal we can share.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync this week with the Redwood ops and partner teams? Prefer afternoons PT.

Hi all — copying in proposed language and ops notes. See attached PDF with redlines on the SOW and a short exhibit draft. High-level points:

1) Commercial exhibit (suggested): define 'Merchant Commission' percentage, clarify whether commission is calculated on list price vs. net collected (we recommend net collected), and specify settlement cadence (we typically do net-45 to allow for marketplace deductions).

2) Evidence for co-sell credits: Microsoft expects entitlement manifests (GUID + SKU + timestamp), purchase receipts from Azure billing (invoice id + charge date), and a consolidated monthly reconciliation CSV from the seller. We'll produce an exportable file that matches the SKU mapping in the attached runbook.

3) Invoice routing: for private offers, invoices are typically routed via the publisher (Redwood) to GreenHelix PO number. For split payments, Microsoft remits to the publisher and the publisher remits the merchant commission per the exhibit. If GreenHelix prefers direct remittance to a sub-merchant, we need to document that in the Marketplace configuration and update the vendor onboarding checklist.

4) Operational runbook items included in attachment: entitlement activation checklist, required evidence fields, expected latencies for entitlement propagation, and contact escalation matrix (Redwood ops, Azure Seller Support, GreenHelix billing).

I attached 'redlines-GHX-priv-plan.pdf' with inline suggestions. Happy to walk through on the call.

—Jonas
Director, Merchant Partnerships
Redwood Inference
